reason: This passage from Exodus 14 depicts the parting of the Red Sea narrative, where the elite Egyptian military force under Pharaoh is defeated and destroyed, while the Israelites—portrayed as enslaved regular people—are saved and vindicated through God's direct intervention. The text explicitly shows the elite being thrown into confusion ('יָהָם אֵת מַחֲנֵה מִצְרַיִם') and destroyed ('וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־ מִצְרַיִם מֵת עַל־ שְׂפַת הַיָּם'), while the regular people are granted salvation and are shown fearing God and believing in the Lord. The narrative structure directly contradicts the notion of elite inherent superiority, instead demonstrating that divine power transcends human social hierarchies.
